questions.q: What are the Fundamental Rights in India?
questions.answer: The Fundamental Rights are the basic rights of the common people and inalienable rights of the people who enjoy it under the charter of rights contained in Part III (Article 12 to 35) of Constitution of India.

questions.q: What civil liberties do the Fundamental Rights guarantee to Indians?
questions.answer: They guarantee civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India, including equality before law, freedom of speech and expression, religious and cultural freedom, peaceful assembly, freedom to practice religion, and the right to constitutional remedies for the protection of civil rights by means of writs such as habeas corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

triples.o: civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India

questions.q: What happens when Fundamental Rights are violated?
questions.answer: Violation of these rights result in punishments as prescribed in the Indian Penal Code or other special laws, subject to discretion of the judiciary.

triples.o: punishments as prescribed in the Indian Penal Code or other special laws, subject to discretion of the judiciary

questions.q: Can the Supreme Court of India be approached directly for violation of Fundamental Rights?
questions.answer: Yes, in case of fundamental rights violation, Supreme court of India can be approached directly for ultimate justice per Article 32.

questions.q: What are the origins of the Fundamental Rights in India?
questions.answer: The Rights have their origins in many sources, including England's Bill of Rights, the United States Bill of Rights and France's Declaration of the Rights of Man.

title: Fundamental rights in India

questions.q: What are Fundamental Rights in India?
questions.answer: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights of the common people and inalienable rights of the people who enjoy it under the charter of rights contained in Part III (Article 12 to 35) of Constitution of India.

triples.o: basic rights of the common people and inalienable rights of the people who enjoy it under the charter of rights contained in Part III (Article 12 to 35) of Constitution of India

questions.q: What does Fundamental rights in India guarantee?
questions.answer: It guarantees civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India.

triples.o: civil liberties such that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India

questions.q: What rights are included in Fundamental rights in India?
questions.answer: These include individual rights common to most liberal democracies, such as equality before law, freedom of speech and expression, religious and cultural freedom and peaceful assembly, freedom to practice religion, and the right to constitutional remedies for the protection of civil rights by means of writs such as habeas corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

triples.o: individual rights common to most liberal democracies, such as equality before law, freedom of speech and expression, religious and cultural freedom and peaceful assembly, freedom to practice religion, and the right to constitutional remedies for the protection of civil rights by means of writs such as habeas corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto

questions.q: What happens when Fundamental rights in India are violated?
questions.answer: Violation of these rights result in punishments as prescribed in the Indian Penal Code or other special laws, subject to discretion of the judiciary.

triples.o: punishments as prescribed in the Indian Penal Code or other special laws, subject to discretion of the judiciary

questions.q: Who can approach the Supreme Court of India directly for fundamental rights violation?
questions.answer: In case of fundamental rights violation, the Supreme Court of India can be approached directly for ultimate justice per Article 32.

questions.q: What are the origins of Fundamental rights in India?
questions.answer: The Rights have their origins in many sources, including England's Bill of Rights, the United States Bill of Rights and France's Declaration of the Rights of Man.
